source: NASA/JPL Small-Body Database API (ssd-api.jpl.nasa.gov/sbdb.api), heliocentric ecliptic J2000 osculating elements

objects.name: ʻOumuamua
objects.note: The first interstellar object ever seen. A tumbling, very elongated body with no visible coma, it sped up slightly as it left the Sun (Micheli et al. 2018, Nature 559, 223). Its name is Hawaiian for "a messenger from afar arriving first".

objects.name: Borisov
objects.by: Gennadiy Borisov, an amateur astronomer (Nauchnij, Crimea)
objects.note: The first interstellar comet: a coma and tail like a Solar System comet, but rich in carbon monoxide (Bodewits et al. 2020, Nature Astronomy 4, 867).

objects.name: 3I/ATLAS
objects.note: The fastest of the three, and perhaps very old: its path suggests it comes from the Milky Way's thick disc, possibly older than the Sun (Seligman et al. 2025; Hopkins et al. 2025).
